findings.reason: §2 must read as an extension of the one production solve, because the node will otherwise port the prototype's solver and §2 done-when (3)'s "ten Newton corrections" will be measured on a loop that is not the one it names.
findings.text: §2's endpoint is a four-line change to `_residual` (`iron = total + MU0*gain*state`, then `state - (fill*coefficient*iron)`) plus `fill` and `gain` carried in the operand tuple that `solve_magnetisation` already packs at `:396-399`, yet the prototype implemented it as a second solver (`axisymmetric.py:109-155,158-226`) that reads `_mesh`, `_average_external`, `_galerkin_interaction` and `_coefficient` out of the owner, so the production solve now has a private-API consumer whose copy will drift from the adaptive regularisation it duplicates; the census of this defect type is this one site — `bricks.py:50`'s rectangle closed form has no owner in nova (`nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py` is the 2D poloidal polygon kernel, not a 3D brick face), so §1 is genuinely new work and only the material rule has an owner to extend

findings.reason: §3 done-when (1) integrates `f` across each section to 1e-3 relative and §2 reports `N`, so the plan must place the derivation in one mechanism or it will be measured against two definitions of its own input.
findings.text: the mapping from machine geometry to the per-cell rule is spread across the caller: `Model.__init__` composes `gain = ((1-fill)/fill)*(1-factor)` at `:164-172`, `limb_demagnetising` at `:94` decides which component takes `N` and is called from two sites (`:259`, `:373`), `flat_fill` at `:333` defines `f` as `min(1, 0.764/R)` while `limb_fraction` at `:50` defines the same `f` as `6/pi*arcsin(0.4/max(R,0.8))`, and the two differ in the hub transition band they clamp over; a deep design takes the limb section and the axis orientation and returns the rule, so `f`, `N` and `gain` are one object rather than three lambdas at every call site

findings.reason: §2 done-when (1) asserts both arms are bit-identical when `f` is omitted, so the plan must state that the production loop and production tile plan carry both arms or that assertion cannot hold.
findings.text: `newton` reproduces `solve_magnetisation`'s acceptance test exactly — the `ratio > 0.25` threshold, the 35 attempts, the x0.3/x2/x10 damping schedule, lambda starting at 1e-6 (`nova/biot/magnetisation.py:408,422-442`) — around a residual the owner could accept as a parameter, and `Model` at `:158` adds nothing but the fill/gain arithmetic over `_mesh`, `_average_external`, `_galerkin_interaction` and `_coefficient`; it also pins its own `TilePlan(128,128,256,16,48)` at `:40` rather than the module default `_PLAN`, so the prototype's interaction and the production solve's are tuned differently and no measurement in §2 can be compared across them without saying which plan produced it

findings.reason: §3 must return the region along with `f` to retire twelve duplicate constructions, and a read that returns only `f` leaves the outline rebuildable and the done-when unmeasurable.
findings.text: `MachineIronSegment` carries `name`, `description`, `outline` and `material` but no region, and no fill fraction, so twelve call sites rebuild the shapely region from `outline.r`/`outline.z` by hand and would each rebuild the true flat outline independently: scripts/west_iron_solve/measure.py:183, scripts/west_iron_solve/diagnose.py:196, scripts/west_iron_solve/probe.py:46, scripts/west_iron_solve/diagnostic_figure.py:39, scripts/west_iron_galerkin/measure.py:231, scripts/west_iron_galerkin_pair/measure.py:351, scripts/west_picard_control/measure.py:338, scripts/west_root_branch/measure.py:235, scripts/west_stray_field/solve.py:76, scripts/sheet_tile_census/measure.py:83, scripts/prototypes/iron_magnetisation/west.py:34, scripts/prototypes/iron_limb_fill/axisymmetric.py:298; §3's endpoint adds `f` to this read and stops there, so done-when (3)'s "no second construction of the flat outline in the tree" is unenforceable — the census is the twelve sites above, and the prototype is the one that already goes furthest, building `flat` at `axisymmetric.py:306-314` and `flat_fill` at `:333` outside the owner

findings.reason: the plan should say in its own text that §2's inputs are the single material-rule surface and that §3's refusal is a tightened existing read, because at zero in all four families this section is where the week's whole interface growth lands.
findings.text: with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0 and refusal_families 0, §3 adds a per-region fill fraction to the machine read and a new refusal ("a stored outline that does not obey thickness times radius constant to 1% is refused by name"), and §2 adds per-cell fill and cross-field inputs to the production material solve; §3's retirement statement covers only the flat-outline construction and nothing about the new record field or the refusal, and §2's states that `f = 1` reproduces the present residual but not whether the new inputs are the only material rule or sit beside the existing full-iron path
